# Temple Scroll Column 67 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 67 | **Condition:** fragmentary (final column)

---

**67:1** Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field.

**67:2** Blessed shall be the fruit of your body, the produce of your soil, and the offspring of your livestock — the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks.

**67:3** Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.

**67:4** Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out.

**67:5** The LORD will cause the enemies who rise against you to be routed before you. They will advance against you from one direction and flee from you in seven directions.

**67:6** But if you do not obey the LORD your God by diligently observing all his commandments and statutes, [...] all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.

**67:7** Cursed shall you be in the city, and cursed shall you be in the field.

**67:8** Cursed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.

**67:9** Cursed shall be the fruit of your body and the produce of your soil, the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks. [...]

**67:10** [...] The LORD will send upon you calamity, panic, and frustration in everything you undertake, until you are destroyed and quickly perish, on account of the evil you have done in forsaking me.

**67:11** [...] The LORD will afflict you with pestilence until he has eliminated you from the land you are about to enter and possess. [...]

**67:12** [...] because you did not serve the LORD your God with joyfulness and gladness of heart for the abundance of all things. [...]

**67:13** [...] you will serve the enemies the LORD sends against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and deprivation of everything. He will place an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you. [...]

**67:14** [...] All these curses shall come upon you, pursuing and overtaking you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the LORD your God and keep the commandments and statutes he gave you. [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 67, the final column of 11Q19, presents the covenant blessings and curses drawn from Deuteronomy 28. The symmetrical structure — blessings in 67:1–5 mirrored by curses in 67:7–9 — is a classic covenant formulary. Heavy damage throughout the curse section; [...] marks genuine lacunae. "Calamity, panic, and frustration" for המארה המהומה והמגערת renders the alliterative Hebrew triad. "Forsaking me" — even in the curses, God speaks in first person. The scroll breaks off mid-curse; the original ending is lost.*
